description: This plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and three different measures of accuracy: Final Accuracy, $\Delta$ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy. The x-axis is labeled "Initial Confidence" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0.81 to 0.99, with labeled tick marks generally spaced at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. The plot displays three lines, all of which feature vertical error bars at each data point. The "Final Accuracy" line is a solid blue line with circular markers; it begins at a value of 1.0 at x=0.81, remains relatively high with minor fluctuations, experiences a low point of approximately 0.87 at x=0.95, and ends at approximately 0.98 at x=0.99. The "$\Delta$ Accuracy" line is a dashed orange line with diamond markers; it starts at approximately 0.46 at x=0.81, exhibits a fluctuating but overall downward trend, dips to approximately 0.14 at x=0.86 and x=0.95, and concludes at its lowest point of approximately 0.04 at x=0.99. The "Initial Accuracy" line is a dash-dot green line with square markers; it begins at approximately 0.54 at x=0.81, shows a fluctuating but generally upward trend, reaches a local peak of approximately 0.76 at x=0.86, and ends at its highest value of approximately 0.94 at x=0.99.
